label: Gatterer 1771 treats outward bodily differences as accidental varieties rather than sufficient evidence of essential difference
subject: agent.johann-christoph-gatterer

sources.citation: André de Melo Araújo, Weltgeschichte in Göttingen (Bielefeld: transcript, 2012), p.153, quoting/reconstructing Johann Christoph Gatterer, Einleitung in die synchronistische Universalhistorie (1771), pp.61-62
Gatterer, Einleitung in die synchronistische Universalhistorie (1771), BSB/MDZ bsb10716342; primary printed pp.61-62 not page-image inspected in Round 4

observations.value: Outward human differences are reported as not wesentliche but zufällige Unterscheidungszeichen and as blose Varietäten.
Visible bodily difference does not by itself license essential difference or proof of multiple separate human origins.

claim_limit: TEXT-DERIVATIVE / NOT PAGE-IMAGE CONTROLLED. Upgrade only after direct inspection of printed pp.61-62; preserve actor wording as secondary-mediated until then.

label: Gatterer 1775 places human bodily shape and colour inside a programmatic geographical Anthropographia
subject: work.gatterer-abriss-geographie.1775
object: Geographie der Menschenkörper nach Gestalt und Farbe/Hautfarbe

sources.citation: Han F. Vermeulen, 2019, quoting Gatterer, Abriß der Geographie (1775), pp.4-5: four-part geography including Menschen- und Völkerkunde (Anthropographia und Ethnographia), explicitly in geographical meaning
Jakob Fischer, Geography and Enlightenment in the German states, c.1690-c.1815 (PhD, 2014), reconstruction of Gatterer 1775 pp.4-5 and Inhaltsanzeige pp.xviii-xxxvi / p.xxxiv

observations.value: Gatterer divides geography into Gränzkunde, Länderkunde, Staatenkunde, and Menschen- und Völkerkunde (Anthropographia und Ethnographia), insisting on geographical rather than historical/political/statistical meanings.
The fourth part programmatically includes a geography of human bodies by shape and colour, with geography of languages treated separately in the adjacent architecture.
The relevant fourth-part architecture is substantially programmatic/outlined rather than a fully executed empirical section of the Abriß.
Secondary witnesses vary between Farben and Hautfarben; exact primary wording remains unresolved pending the contents-leaf image.

claim_limit: TEXT-DERIVATIVE / NOT PAGE-IMAGE CONTROLLED. This supports descriptive geographical use of bodily colour, not essential, causal, or genealogical authority.

label: Gatterer 1789 gives language stronger warrant than bodily colour for the origin and division of peoples
subject: work.gatterer-kurzer-begriff-geographie.vol2.1789

sources.citation: Araújo 2012, pp.143-144, citing Gatterer, Kurzer Begriff der Geographie, vol.2 (1789), p.606
Gatterer, Kurzer Begriff der Geographie, vol.2 (1789), BSB/DDB carrier; p.606 not page-image inspected in Round 4

observations.value: African peoples are reported as divided in Rücksicht auf die Hauptsprachen, welche sie reden; language is reconstructed as the stronger evidence of origin.
Araújo interprets residual skin-colour division as fallback where genauen und zuverlässigen Nachrichten about language are unavailable.

claim_limit: TEXT-DERIVATIVE / NOT PAGE-IMAGE CONTROLLED. The fallback-under-linguistic-data-scarcity formulation is secondary interpretation, not currently controlled as direct Gatterer wording.

label: Gatterer separates perceptual visibility, descriptive classification, essential difference, and genealogical origin as distinct inference jurisdictions

observations.value: Outward bodily differences may be visible varieties without establishing essential difference or separate origin.
Bodily shape and colour remain legitimate programmatic variables for geographical Anthropographia.
Language carries stronger genealogical/origin warrant than bodily colour, with colour's fallback role currently secondary-mediated.
perceptual discriminability != descriptive classificatory utility != essential inference != genealogical inference

claim_limit: Comparative synthesis from text-derivative controls. Do not upgrade to primary_direct until the residual page packet is visually inspected.

label: No actor-level bridge established from Gatterer's anthropographic bodily colour to heraldic or synchronistic-table colour regimes
notes: Repository search and existing primary/secondary controls show distinct Gatterer/Göttingen colour regimes in heraldry, synchronistic/tabular display, and human bodily description. No actor-level statement currently links them by transfer, derivation, common colour method, or shared inference rule.

observations.value: cross-domain comparison remains analytically useful for testing display, coding, description and inference jurisdiction

reopen_rule: Reopen only if a direct Gatterer cross-reference, methodological statement, correspondence, lecture note, or publication instruction explicitly connects the colour regimes. Shared use of colour alone is insufficient.
